given: a stock record already exists for a given SKU at a given location
when: the operator files that same SKU at that same location again with a different quantity and tracking code
then: the existing record is updated in place to the newly filed values, no second record for that (sku, location) pair is created, and no error page is shown
architectural_notes: E2E: same boundary -> service -> repository -> models path as AC1, but the collision case. The service (app/services/stock_service.py) owns the upsert-on-collision decision (resolve the existing (sku, location) row and update in place) and its transaction; the repository (app/repositories/stock_repository.py) does the ORM read+write against app/models/stock_record.py. Directly defends persistence invariant PI1 (unique composite key on (sku, location)) so no duplicate is ever stored and the collision surfaces as an update, not a DB error page. Verified against the real paired-branch DB (R4), never a mock.

independence.rationale: AC1 asserts a brand-new record is persisted and readable; AC2 asserts the collision case, that a repeat filing of the same (sku, location) pair updates the single record rather than producing a duplicate or an error, an outcome AC1 never exercises.
